public_rationale: The evidence shows concentrated general cloud services and operating AI infrastructure suppliers outside the four named firms. CoreWeave and Oracle undermine a literal exclusivity claim. They do not, by themselves, disprove the ordinary contextual claim of effective collective control. The available measurements do not match the AI-capacity and GPU-access market needed to settle that claim.
limitations: Cloud revenue shares are a different measure from physical capacity or GPU access.
Company announcements establish activity, not independently measured market power.
A literal exclusivity reading would produce a different assessment.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Microsoft, Google, Amazon and Meta monopolize AI infrastructure, through data centers and access to the GPUs needed to run models.

statement.excerpt: Microsoft, Google, Amazon and Meta also monopolize the infrastructure itself, both in the data centers they can build (or already own) and in their access to the specialized GPUs necessary to run these models.

from_speaker: data centers they can build (or already own)
access to the specialized GPUs necessary to run these models
our_interpretation: The ordinary contextual reading is effective collective control of infrastructure for large-scale model training and operation, sufficient to obstruct independent competition.
This does not require literal ownership of every data center or GPU. Conversely, a majority share of general cloud revenue does not by itself establish control of AI infrastructure.
Use calendar Q2 2024, the latest completed quarter that could have been reported before the post, for the undated ongoing state.
The claim supplies no geographical limit; the comparison is worldwide.
criteria.support_condition: AI-specific capacity, GPU-access, and commercial-access evidence establishes effective collective control by the four firms over competitive large-scale model infrastructure.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence establishes material independent infrastructure and GPU access at competitive scale, sufficient to show that the four firms did not exercise the claimed collective control.

evidence.locator: First substantive paragraph; Amazon, Microsoft, and Google
evidence.explanation: The figures show substantial concentration in general cloud infrastructure services. They do not measure AI data-center capacity, Meta's infrastructure, or access to specialized GPUs.

CoreWeave reported a substantial operating footprint as a specialized GPU-cloud supplier. This challenges an exclusive-control reading, but the disclosure does not establish its market share or how much capacity was independently available.

Oracle reported existing AI customers outside the four named infrastructure suppliers. The announced OpenAI capacity extension involved Microsoft, so this does not establish independence of every workload or disprove collective market power.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Q2 2024 AI-specific capacity and GPU-access measurements, including contractually controlled capacity and independent customers' ability to obtain competitive service.
